caveat: n=1 offset per method class; the break-even is indicative, not a proven threshold
conclusion: the local-selection bias against the analog family was real but did not cost a better candidate: the family's best falls short of the break-even
coverage_note: only M244 and M251 have full Q2-Q4 persistence in the analog family; all Q3-only variants were rejected against M244 or its parents, so M244 is the family's best dev-surface candidate. M245 equals M244 on the dev surface because its change is confined to Q1.
logic: an offset constant within a method class cannot reorder that class; it only shifts cross-class comparison. So the operation is a break-even test, not a re-rank.
